Commentary.Commentary: The players are back out in the middle. Tom Latham and Devon Conway begin their mission of handing New Zealand their first Test series win in England this century. Their last series win here was way back in 1999. Here's James Anderson to Tom Latham.
... FINAL INNINGS ...

Right then. What can England make of this small target? A couple of wickets perhaps? Maybe put some clouds into the thought process of the Kiwis ahead of the World Test Championship Final? Don't think Tom Latham and Devon Conway would be in any sort of hurry to get these under-40 runs. Stay tuned for the final innings of the match.

As per our clocks and I am sure, as per your clocks, the match started exactly at 11 am local (1000 GMT). But now the camera pans onto the official clock on the ground. The game has to begin as per that clock, not any other. It is 10.59 am on that clock. The umpires could come into question at the end of the match for this premature start, though that is just for argument. Don't think it would really have mattered much even if they had started post 11 am. Just something to chew...

No time wastage. They came, they saw and they wrapped it up. No wagging of the tail. If England fans were hoping for SOME sort of batting ecstacy, they have been totally denied. A strange eerie has descended at Edgbaston, as if this were the Ashes. But hang on, there could be some controversy.

OUT! CAUGHT BEHIND! One ball. That is all it has taken. On a length, around off, angling away, Olly Stone looks to push but the away movement does him in. A thin outside edge and keeper Tom Blundell does the rest. NEW ZEALAND NEED 38 TO WIN!
Commentary.Howout: c Tom Blundell b Trent Boult

Commentary.Commentary: The players are out in the middle then. A pacer to start. Here's Trent Boult ​​​to Olly Stone. 10-2-34-1 so far.

New Zealand would be very happy. Not just because of this bowling performance as a whole, but because their missing pieces getting joined. Neil Wagner was looking a bit out of sorts in the first Test, but with 6 wickets in this one, he has tuned himself nicely for the Word Test Championship final against India, starting the coming Friday. The batting looks good and even the spin options are nicely stocked up. So all in readiness for the grand finale. For today, they would want to wrap up this innings as quickly as possible and win the match by the end of the session, at the most. It will be interesting to see who bowls the first over. Normally tailenders like to slog against spinners. Would Tom Latham open with Ajaz Patel at one end and one of the seamers at the other? Stay tuned for the action to begin.

What ails England? Batting and catching. They had New Zealand in trouble when the lead was slender but then dropped a few catches again to let them off the hook. And then with the bat, they once again played too many shots to get out of contention of the match as a whole. They lead by just 37 and only have Olly Stone and James Anderson in the middle. Looking at Anderson's batting credentials, Stone might just throw his bat around and try and get as many runs as possible. For England's sake, if Jimmy can channelise his Nottingham innings of 2014, against India, it would be very handy. England were 298/9 there and Joe Root and James Anderson forged a partnership of hold your breath - 198 - yes, that's right. 198, for the last wicket, of which Jimmy scored 81. Can they emulate something of that stand? For now, even a target of 100 would give some respect to this English team.

Refreshed? Sleep done? Fully awake? Okay. Time to pinch yourself again. Yes. This is not the highlights package of any match. England are actually 9 down, having lost 7 wickets in a session. Had it not been for Mark Wood, who played an entertaining cameo of 29 in 38 balls, we might have actually seen the game finish off on Saturday itself. A day to forget for England. A nightmare. They are on the cusp of a match and series defeat and it should only be a matter of time before the game is done. On that note, hello and a warm welcome to what is the fourth day, but could be the final day, final session or even the final hour of the second Test between England and New Zealand at Edgbaston, Birmingham.

Now then, what can we expect on Day 4? England will need a miracle to win this one but a miracle just does not seem possible. New Zealand will want to take the last wicket quickly and then score the runs off. Don't think Day 4 will last for more than a session. Do join us for all the action. Till then, take care and goodbye!

Matt Henry started things off with two wickets just before the Tea break. He then got another after the break. After that, every bowler chipped in. Wagner also took 3, Ajaz for two and Boult one. Had it not been for Stone and Wood, England might have already lost this game. Have to say, it is a sorry batting effort from the hosts and an excellent effort form the visitors with the ball.

The first one and a half sessions did not completely belong to them. From a position where it looked like they would take a big lead, they only got one just above 80. However, it was all about their bowlers after that.
End of an outstanding day for the visitors! More or less, they have sealed the deal (series) with the performance they have displayed on Day 3.

Still 9 away from wiping off the deficit.

... Day 3, Session 3 ...

So, England have lost two in the 6 overs they had to face before the break and are on the back foot! Henry has been the one causing problems as he has got not the openers. The hosts still trail by over 60 and a lot will depend on Root if they are to find a way out of this tough situation. He'll need support from the others and especially Crawley who is in need of some runs. Can he deliver?

Talking about the session now, it has been a good one for the bowlers. 7 wickets have fallen in total. 5 for the Kiwiss and two of England. Not good sings if you're an English fan as that just indicates that batting is getting tough. The wicket though seems to be playing well. We'll find out more after the break. Will we see ball dominate again?
